The following is a list of [[stats]] in ''[[Final Fantasy Tactics]]''. Stats applies to all [[Unit (term)|units]], both [[Final Fantasy Tactics characters|party members]] and [[Final Fantasy Tactics enemies|enemies]].

The stat names vary in different [[Final Fantasy Tactics version differences|versions]]. Some stats are listed alongside each other in ''[[Final Fantasy Tactics: The War of the Lions|The War of the Lions]]'', but together in ''[[Final Fantasy Tactics: The Ivalice Chronicles|The Ivalice Chronicles]]''.

The stats can be broadly divided into Primary Stats (HP, MP, Speed, Physical Attack, and Magickal Attack) which grow at level-up based on complex mechanics, and other stats which are either fixed, situational, or modified by equipment and abilities.

== List of stats ==
=== Primary stats ===
These five stats are governed by the [[#Stat growth mechanics|growth mechanics, raw stats, and job modifiers]] detailed in the next section.

==== [[HP (stat)|HP]] ====
A measure of the unit's life. When a unit's HP is reduced to zero, he or she is [[KO (Tactics)|KO'd]]. The amount of HP gained on level up corresponds to the job class they were in. [[Mime (Tactics)|Mime]], [[Knight (Tactics)|knight]], and [[Dragoon (Tactics)|dragoon]] jobs typically raise the most HP, whereas [[Bard (Tactics)|bard]] and [[Dancer (Tactics)|dancer]] gain the least. Equipping certain [[Final Fantasy Tactics armor|armor and helmets]] also raises max HP. The maximum HP a unit can theoretically attain is 999. Boss monsters, namely the [[Lucavi]], can exceed 999 HP.

HP can be restored in battle using the help of items, magick, and other abilities, such as in the [[Chakra (Tactics)|Chakra]] action ability of the [[Monk (Tactics)|monk]], and by picking up crystals left by [[KO (Tactics)|defeated units]]. [[Lifefont (Tactics)|Lifefont]] restores HP by moving and [[Regen (Tactics status)|Regen]] also restores health passively on a unit's turn. Some recovery abilities' and items' effects are reversed on [[undead]] targets, so they will deal damage instead of providing healing. HP/MP are fully restored after the end of each battle.

==== [[MP (stat)|MP]] ====
These points are used to cast magicks. A unit's MP depends on which job they are currently using and which jobs they have used in the past, as the stat growth depends on the jobs in use at the time of the level up. Mage type jobs have a much greater MP gain than melee jobs.

Mage equipment gives more MP to the wearer. [[Manafont (Tactics)|Manafont]] restores some MP to the unit when they move during their turn, and [[Mana Shield (Tactics)|Mana Shield]] protects the unit by deducting MP rather than HP when damaged.

==== [[Speed (stat)|Speed]] ====
A combination of the unit's inherent speed and any job, equipment, or ability bonuses. A higher number means the unit's turn will come more quickly, as it determines how fast the [[#CT|CT]] gauge fills.

Speed also affects the damage dealt by [[Knives (Tactics)|knives]], [[Bows (Tactics)|bows]], [[Ninja blades (Tactics)|ninja blades]] and the [[Ninja (Tactics)|ninja]]'s [[Throw (Tactics)|Throw]]. The stat also affects the chance of success of the [[Machinist (Tactics)|machinist]]'s [[Aimed Shot (Tactics)|Aimed Shot]], the [[Thief (Tactics)|thief]]'s [[Steal (Tactics)|Steal]] and the [[Sky Pirate (Tactics)|sky pirate]]'s Plunder (except for [[Steal Heart (Tactics)|Steal Heart]] and [[Plunder Heart]], respectively), the latter being exclusive to ''The War of the Lions'' version.

==== Physical Attack ====
Known as "{{A|ATK}}" (top number) in ''The War of the Lions''. 

Physical attack sums the unit's total physical attack attribute, combining the base stat with any bonuses from their job, abilities, or equipment. It is a key factor in determining damage from physical attacks.

==== Magick Attack ====
Known as "{{A|ATK}}" (bottom number) in ''The War of the Lions''.

This sums the unit's total magick attack attribute, combining the base stat with any equipment, job, or ability. It is a key factor in determining damage, healing and success rate from most magickal abilities.

Magickal attack also affects the damage dealt by [[Books (Tactics)|books]], [[Cloths (Tactics)|cloths]], [[Instruments (Tactics)|instruments]], [[Poles (Tactics)|poles]] and [[Staves (Tactics)|staves]].

=== Secondary stats ===
These stats are fundamental to a unit's progression and action in battle, but are not governed by the raw stat growth formulas.

==== [[Level|Lv.]] ====
Indicates the unit's level, which increases by 1 for every 100 experience points earned (or from [[Bequeath Bacon]] monster ability). The maximum level is 99. A unit's level grants EXP based on the target's level; 10 EXP is granted for a same-level target, with ±1 EXP for each level of difference. The abilities [[EXP bonus abilities#Final Fantasy Tactics|Accrue EXP and EXP Boost]] can be equipped to gain more EXP.

==== [[Experience Points|EXP]] ====
A numerical representation of the unit's experience. EXP is gained by using command abilities on any target (friend, foe, or self). More EXP is gained when targeting higher-level units. The [[EXP Boost (Tactics)|EXP Boost]] ability increases EXP gain. Units will not gain experience if their action is not significant (e.g. healing a unit at full HP). [[Accrue EXP]] allows the unit to gain EXP just by moving. When EXP reaches 100, the unit levels up and the counter resets to 0, regardless of any overflow. EXP is not gained during multiplayer mode in the PSP version. EXP also has a minor effect on the success of [[errands]].

==== [[Ability Points|JP]] & Job Level ====
A numerical representation of the unit's [[Final Fantasy Tactics jobs|job]] points, which are used to unlock abilities, as well other jobs. Once a unit has accrued enough JP on a specific job, said job will increase in level (which is separate from the unit's own level). Each job has its own JP amount from each other; this means that the JP earned in the [[Squire (Tactics)|squire]] job will not be the same as the JP earned in the [[Chemist (Tactics)|chemist]] job. The maximum amount of JP each job can hold is 9,999.

A unit gains JP by successfully performing an action, such as dealing damage to an enemy, or healing themselves or an ally. Units will not gain JP if the action is not successful, such as missing an attack or healing while at full HP. Generic units can also be sent into errands, which will reward them with different amounts of JP depending on the success of the mission.

The amount of JP earned per action scales with the unit's job level. This accrual can be enhanced with the [[JP Boost (Tactics)|JP Boost]] [[Final Fantasy Tactics support abilities|support ability]] from the [[Squire (Tactics)|squire]] and other special jobs (e.g. [[Holy Knight (Tactics)|holy knight]], [[Machinist (Tactics)|machinist]]), and the [[Accrue JP]] [[Final Fantasy Tactics movement abilities|movement ability]] from the [[Arithmetician (Tactics)|arithmetician]] (which is also affected by JP Boost). The bonus granted from JP Boost will not affect the JP earned in errands.

In ''The Ivalice Chronicles'' version, players who purchased the Deluxe Edition will have access to the [[Ring of Aptitude|ring of aptitude]], an [[Final Fantasy Tactics accessories|accessory]] that provides the same effect as JP Boost. While this ring and the support ability do not stack, this frees the support ability of an unit to use other valuable abilities; an example of this is [[Cidolfus Orlandeau]], who can use the [[Knight (Tactics)|knight]]'s [[Equip Swords (Tactics)|Equip Swords]] to use his devastating techniques from the [[Sword Saint (Tactics)|sword saint]] job while leveling up in another job, and still retain the bonus JP from the ring of aptitude.

A mechanic referred to as "JP spillover" is a passive share effect where active party members in battle receive 25% of the JP earned by any other ally for that specific job, regardless of their own current job. The spillover amount is calculated from the base JP earned, and is not affected by the bonus from JP Boost & ring of aptitude. Spillover JP accumulate in the background for locked jobs and become visible and usable the moment the player finally meet the requirements to unlock that job. This means that, for example, if [[Ramza Beoulve]] is accruing JP for the [[Samurai (Tactics)|samurai]] job while [[Agrias Oaks]] is in the battle, but has not unlocked samurai yet, the hidden spillover JP she gained will be available once she unlocks the samurai job. Units will not accrue spillover JP under all status effects (including [[Stone (Tactics status)|Stone]]), except for [[KO (Tactics)|KO]]. 

In the original PlayStation version, there is a [[JP scroll glitch]] that allows the player obtain 9,999 JP without effort for certain jobs.

Monster units do not earn JP.

==== [[Charge time|CT]] ====
Indicates the amount of time a unit must wait between turns. The unit cannot take a turn until its CT reaches 100. All battle units and most spells/abilities have a CT. Direct attacks and some skills do not require charging. A unit's [[#Speed (stat)|Speed]] determines how fast the CT gauge fills (CT gain per "tick" = Speed).

After a turn, CT is reduced: by 100 for moving and acting, by 80 for moving or acting, and by 60 for waiting. Leftover CT caps at 60 before recharging.

Abilities that require charging use a separate, hidden CT gauge based on the ability's own speed, which is not affected by the user's speed, [[Haste (Tactics status)|Haste]], or [[Slow (Tactics status)|Slow]] (except for [[Jump (Tactics)|Jump]]). [[Stop (Tactics status)|Stop]] will halt this charge.

If a unit's turn comes up while charging an ability, they must choose "Wait" to continue charging, or the ability will be canceled. While charging (except for Jump), a unit cannot evade and takes ~50% extra physical damage.

Abilities like [[Haste (Tactics)|Haste]] (increases speed) and [[Quick (Tactics)|Quick]] (sets CT to 100) can manipulate the CT gauge.

CT is also a special command ability for the [[Arithmetician (Tactics)|Arithmetician]], allowing magick to target units based on their current CT value.

=== Combat stats ===
Bravery and faith govern percentages and effectiveness for many actions in combat. They do not grow with levels but are modified by specific abilities.

==== [[Bravery (stat)|Bravery]] ====
{{main|Bravery (Tactics)}}
This number indicates how brave the unit is. It directly represents the percentage chance of [[Final Fantasy Tactics reaction abilities|reaction abilities]] activating, except for the [[Knight (Tactics)|knight]]'s [[Parry (Tactics)|Parry]] and the [[Ninja (Tactics)|ninja]]'s [[Reflexes (Tactics)|Reflexes]]. Bravery also affects the [[Chemist (Tactics)|chemist's]] [[Treasure Hunter (Tactics)|Treasure Hunter]] [[Final Fantasy Tactics movement abilities|movement ability]]. If a unit's max bravery is 5 or below at the end of a battle, they will leave the party permanently (Ramza is the only character who will never leave).

Bravery also affects the damage dealt by [[Katana (Tactics)|katana]] and [[Knight's swords (Tactics)|knight's swords]], as well bare hands and the [[Monk (Tactics)|monk]]'s [[Brawler (Tactics)|Brawler]] [[Final Fantasy Tactics support abilities|support ability]]. 

==== [[Faith (stat)|Faith]] ====
{{main|Faith (stat)}}
Faith is a measure (in percentage) of a character's belief in the divine, and impacts the effectiveness of their magicks. A high faith stat is double-edged: units with higher faith will deal higher magickal damage and healing, but will also receive increased damage and healing from magicks, are more susceptible to magickal [[Final Fantasy Tactics statuses|status effect]] spells, and take increased damage from elemental guns. Most spells compute the faith scores of both caster and target. Zero faith (or the [[Atheist]] status) will render all magick unsuccessful. If a unit's max faith is 95 or higher at the end of a battle, they will leave the party permanently (Ramza is the only character who will never leave).

Faith also affects the damage of [[Guns (Tactics)|magick guns]], as well [[Fell swords (Tactics)|fell swords]] in ''The War of the Lions'' version.

=== Derived and equipment stats ===
These stats are determined by a unit's Job, equipped items, and equipped abilities, not by level growth.

==== [[Move (stat)|Movement]] ====
Known as "{{A|Move}}" in ''The War of the Lions''.

A combination of the unit's base movement range and any job, equipment, or ability bonuses. The higher the number, the farther the unit can move.

==== [[Jump (stat)|Jump]] ====
A combination of the unit's base jumping ability and any job, equipment, or ability bonuses. This attribute governs how many tiles the unit can jump horizontally, as well as how far up or down a slope the unit can jump.

==== Physical Evasion ====
Listed as the top number under "{{A|C-EV}}" in ''The War of the Lions''.

Refers to the unit's ability to evade a physical attack. It sums up their base evasion rate and any bonuses from a job, equipment, or ability. 

==== Magickal Evasion ====
Listed as the bottom number under "C-EV" in ''The War of the Lions''.

Refers to the unit's ability to evade a magick attack. It sums up their base evasion rate and any bonuses from a job, equipment, or ability.

==== Weapon Attack ====
Known as "{{A|Weapon Power}}" in ''The War of the Lions''.

Refers purely to the bonus attack power granted by the equipped weapon. Represented with (R) and (L) for right and left hands.

==== Weapon Parry ====
In ''The War of the Lions'', it is listed alongside Weapon Power on the right number.

Refers to the weapon's chance to parry an attack. Represented with (R) and (L) for right and left hands.

A unit can only perform a weapon parry if equipped with the knight's Parry reaction ability.

==== Shield Physical Parry ====
Listed as the top number under "{{A|S-EV}}" in ''The War of the Lions''.

The chance the equipped shield provides in blocking a physical attack. 

==== Shield Magickal Parry ====
Listed as the bottom number under "S-EV" in ''The War of the Lions''.

The chance the equipped shield provides in blocking a magick attack.

==== Cloak Physical Evasion ====
Listed as the top number under "{{A|A-EV}}" in ''The War of the Lions''.

The chance that an accessory (like a cloak) can evade a physical attack.

==== Cloak Magickal Evasion ====
Listed as the bottom number under "A-EV" in ''The War of the Lions''.

The chance that an accessory (like a cloak) can evade a magick attack.

== Stat growth mechanics ==
The stat growth of the player characters in ''Final Fantasy Tactics'' is governed by their gender and [[Final Fantasy Tactics jobs|jobs]] they use in [[Battle (term)|battle]]. This system applies to the five [[#Primary stats|primary stats]]: HP, MP, Speed, PA, and MA.

=== Raw stats vs. displayed stats ===
Each unit has five "Raw Stats" the game saves to determine the base stats the player never sees. These Raw Stats are multiplied by the job constants (Multipliers) to determine the unit's final, displayed stats.

The game takes the background raw stats, and uses the following equations to get the base stats:
:<math>HP = [(RawHP \times ClassHPMultiplier) / 1638400]</math>
:<math>MP = [(RawMP \times ClassMPMultiplier) / 1638400]</math>
:<math>Sp = [(RawSp \times ClassSpMultiplier) / 1638400]</math>
:<math>PA = [(RawPA \times ClassPAMultiplier) / 1638400]</math>
:<math>MA = [(RawMA \times ClassMAMultiplier) / 1683400]</math>
:If the final value is less than 1, it becomes 1.

Enemy zodiac beasts, in the special story battles where they are fought, have unique equations that determine their HP and MP:
:<math>HP = [(RawHP \times ClassHPMultiplier) / 163840]</math>
:<math>MP = [(RawMP \times ClassMPMultiplier) / 163840]</math>

The division by 163,840 instead of by 1,638,400 accounts for the zodiac beasts' extremely high HP and MP despite their unremarkable multipliers.

==== Raw stat initial values ====
For [[human]] units, the raw stat at level 1 is a constant for each gender for the Sp, PA, and MA stats. For monsters, which are all one gender and are neither male nor female, only Sp is not random. The following tables explain how to determine the raw stats of a character.

[[Ramza Beoulve]] is the exception, as he starts with 81,920 of both RPA and RMA (but otherwise is a normal male).

Raw HP and raw MP for each unit is randomized within a certain range.

Bred monsters seem to have their raw stats selected at once from a set of 250-500 preset stat configurations. Bred monsters can have bravery and faith ranging from 40 to 70, slightly lower than randomly-generated monsters and units found in battle, which can have bravery and faith ranging from 45 to 74.<ref>[https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/ps/197339-final-fantasy-tactics/faqs/3876 Battle Mechanics Guide (PS) by AeroStar]</ref>

=== Multipliers and growth ===
Multipliers (labeled "M" in the [[#Job breakdown|Job breakdown table]]) are class-specific constants that mostly fall between 50 and 200. Differences in multipliers are what make the differences in the strengths and weaknesses of ''Final Fantasy Tactics'' jobs—a [[Dragoon (Tactics)|dragoon]], for instance, has a high PA multiplier but a low MA multiplier. Differences in multipliers are generally more significant for the surface stats than differences in growth rates.

There are some consequences of the initial raw stat distribution:
*Females gain more MP and MA on level up than males.
*Males gain more HP and PA on level up than females.
*Monsters gain more HP, PA, and MA than either human sex.
*Monsters gain less MP and Speed than either human sex.

=== Leveling up ===
Raw HP, Raw MP, Raw Sp, Raw PA, and Raw MA are all increased on level up, even when there is no visible increase in the corresponding surface stat. Different classes get different raw stat bonuses on level up, which results in the classes' differing stat growth.

Raw stat growth on leveling up is determined by the following equation:
:<math>bonus = [current_RX / (C + Lv)]</math>

"R" is a generic term for any raw stat (Raw HP, Raw MP, Raw Sp, Raw PA, or Raw MA), "Lv" is the level the unit just was, so if the unit is leveling up from 50 to 51, Lv = 50. "C" is a constant that varies for each class (labeled "C" in the [[#Job breakdown|job breakdown table]]). The value of C is what differentiates one class's growth pattern from another's. Since C is in the denominator of this expression, lower values of C yield higher stats.

=== Leveling down ===
Players can use the 'level up/down' trick to build characters with super stats. The idea behind the trick is that the unit levels up in a job with strong stat growth (low C values) such as [[Ninja (Tactics)|ninja]] or [[Mime (Tactics)|mime]], and then levels down using [[Mindflayer (Tactics)|mindflayer's]] Level Blast technique, or one of the many Degenerator [[Trap (term)#Final Fantasy Tactics|traps]] scattered throughout the game's battlefields, with a class with poor stat growth (high C values), such as [[Bard (Tactics)|bard]] or [[Dancer (Tactics)|dancer]]. Though the game adjusts the unit's stats when it levels down so that the player loses the stats that they would have gained as that class, by using poor classes to level down the player can fool the game and lose less going down than the unit gains going up; in this manner, the player can build all the stats up to their maxima if they do enough leveling cycles.

If a unit levels up and down without changing classes, it will actually lower their stats, because the level down algorithm is the following equation:
:<math>decrement = [current RX / (Lv + C)]</math>

Lv is the level the unit is leveling down to. For instance, if a unit levels down to 50 from level 51, Lv = 50. However, if the player changes classes while leveling down, this small loss of stats will be compensated for by the higher C values of the poor stat-gaining class that the unit levels down in.

== Job stat reference tables ==
A character's job affects their current stats via Multipliers (M-Values) and their permanent stat growth via Growth Constants (C-Values). For C-Values, a *lower* number results in *better* growth.

=== Stat growth rates ===
This table reflects the C-Values (Growth Constants). More stars mean a lower C-Value and thus faster stat growth.

=== Job breakdown ===
This table details the specific multipliers (M) and growth constants (C) for each job, as used in the formulas in the [[#Stat growth mechanics|stat growth mechanics]] section.
* **M (Multiplier):** Determines the job's current stats based on Raw Stats. Higher is better.
* **C (Constant):** Determines the job's stat growth on level-up. Lower is better.

Note that Ramza and Cloud in the original US translation have different stats from the Japanese and PSP versions. This table reflects their US PS1 stats.
